supporting_quotes.exact: A linked list is a fundamental data structure in computer science. It mainly allows efficient insertion and deletion operations compared to arrays. Like arrays, it is also used to implement other data structures like stack, queue and deque.

observations.subject: linked list
observations.object: a fundamental data structure in computer science, allowing efficient insertion/deletion compared to arrays, and used like arrays to implement stack, queue and deque

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-d38ddbbef35a（全引文区间 [0,242)）逐句对应该 claim 的三部分："a fundamental data structure in computer science"（[0,65)）对应"基础数据结构"；"allows efficient insertion and deletion operations compared to arrays"（[77,147)）对应"相比数组主要优势是高效的插入与删除"；"used to implement other data structures like stack, queue and deque"（[176,242)）对应"用于实现栈、队列、双端队列等其他数据结构"。claim 无超出引文的额外断言。

supporting_quotes.exact: A linked list is a type of linear data structure individual items are not necessarily at contiguous locations. The individual items are called nodes and connected with each other using links.

observations.subject: linked list
observations.object: a linear data structure whose individual items are not necessarily at contiguous locations; items are called nodes and connected with each other using links

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-2e3920cc1316（全引文区间 [0,191)）完整支撑 claim 各要素："a type of linear data structure"（[0,49)）对应"线性数据结构"；"individual items are not necessarily at contiguous locations"（[66,109)）对应"各元素不必存放在连续位置"；"The individual items are called nodes and connected with each other using links"（[126,191)）对应"元素称为节点，彼此用链接相连"。引文自身缺少修饰词不影响语义对应，无超出引文的断言。

supporting_quotes.exact: - A node contains two things first is data and second is a link that connects it with another node.

In its most basic form, each node contains data, and a reference (in other words, a link) to the next node in the sequence. This structure allows for efficient insertion or removal of elements from any position in the sequence during iteration.

observations.subject: node (in a linked list)
observations.object: two things: data, and a link that connects it with another node

observations.subject: node (in a linked list)
observations.object: data and a reference (a link) to the next node in the sequence

claims.rationale: 两条引文分别覆盖 claim 两个分句：evidence-5fa7b97efee5（[0,99)）"A node contains two things first is data and second is a link that connects it with another node"（[3,99)）直接对应"每个节点包含两样东西——数据与连接到另一节点的链接"；evidence-6f9055c4a223（[0,244)）"each node contains data, and a reference (in other words, a link) to the next node in the sequence"（[25,123)）对应"指向下一个节点的链接"，单数形式及"In its most basic form"语境支持"只持有一个"（"只"属合理弱推理，两引文间无冲突）。

supporting_quotes.exact: - The first node is called the head node and we can traverse the whole list using this head and next links.

observations.subject: first node
observations.object: the head node; the whole list can be traversed using this head and next links

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-a5a4fd131352（全引文区间 [0,107)）与 claim 逐项对应："The first node is called the head node"（[3,41)）对应"第一个节点称为头节点"；"we can traverse the whole list using this head and next links"（[45,107)）对应"借助 head 与 next 链接可以遍历整条链表"。无超出引文的断言。

supporting_quotes.exact: Arrays have better cache locality compared to linked lists.

observations.subject: arrays
observations.object: better cache locality than linked lists

claims.rationale: claim 主句有直接引文支撑：evidence-55fba6124609（[0,31)）"Insertion/Deletion: Efficient"对应"链表的插入/删除高效"；evidence-f7b8487bda5d（[0,20)）"Access: Sequential"对应"访问是顺序的"。但括号内"对比数组：连续存储、随机访问、插删低效"证据不足：evidence-5f4608cd28e0（[0,59)）仅陈述"Arrays have better cache locality"，只能由缓存局部性推出数组连续存储；"数组随机访问"与"数组插删低效"没有任何引文直接陈述，仅由链表侧属性（Sequential、Efficient）反推，属对比推断而非引文明示。故 claim 的数组对比部分超出引文可直接断定的范围。

supporting_quotes.exact: A drawback of linked lists is that data access time is linear with respect to the number of nodes in the list.

Because nodes are serially linked, accessing any node requires that the prior node be accessed beforehand (which introduces difficulties in pipelining). Faster access, such as random access (direct access), is not possible.

observations.subject: linked list
observations.object: data access time linear with respect to the number of nodes in the list

observations.subject: linked list node access
observations.object: prior node accessed beforehand (nodes serially linked); random access (direct access) is not possible

claims.rationale: 两条引文互补支撑 claim 各要素：evidence-e1c0317667fd（[0,110)）"data access time is linear with respect to the number of nodes"（[47,110)）对应"访问时间与节点数成线性关系"；evidence-debf304f8906（[0,223)）"Because nodes are serially linked, accessing any node requires that the prior node be accessed beforehand"（[0,105)）对应"需要从头遍历到目标节点、无直接访问"（串行链接隐含从头部开始），"random access (direct access), is not possible"（[160,223)）对应"无法随机访问"。两引文一致无冲突。

supporting_quotes.exact: The principal benefit of a linked list over a conventional array is that the list elements can be easily inserted or removed without reallocation or reorganization of the entire structure because the data items do not need to be stored contiguously in memory or on disk, while restructuring an array at run-time is a much more expensive operation.

observations.subject: linked list
observations.object: principal benefit over a conventional array: easy insertion/removal without reallocation or reorganization, because data items need not be stored contiguously; restructuring an array at run-time is much more expensive

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-816e76e0295f（全引文区间 [0,347)）完整覆盖 claim 各要素："The principal benefit of a linked list over a conventional array"（[0,72)）对应"相比常规数组的核心好处"；"inserted or removed without reallocation or reorganization of the entire structure"（[98,188)）对应"插入或移除元素无需重新分配或重组整个结构"；"data items do not need to be stored contiguously"（[200,248)）对应"数据项不需要连续存储"；"restructuring an array at run-time is a much more expensive operation"（[277,347)）对应"运行时重组数组代价高得多"。
